answer: The protocol enforces identity via a 512GB memory-hard working set requirement, ensuring honest nodes reach consensus while 1,000 fakes stall as they fail to return the signal of a valid computational state. A verifier challenges agents with random data requests; failure to return the tide of a consistent memory response at the summit of the required cache window triggers an immediate penalty. This memory-latency check forces each agent to maintain high-bandwidth throughput. Honest agents pay 150 watts, while 1,000 fakes incur 150,000 watts, rendering pooling infeasible.
